note:
Shared decision vectors for CANT-31's client rules (CANT-35 ruling 6 → A, built by CANT-156).

The rules are implemented three times: internal/client (the Go reference), web/src/transport (TypeScript) and CANT-42's Dart. If two of them disagree, a device stops when it should reconnect, or keeps minting refresh links on a dead network, and neither is a type error. So every language's tests read THIS file and must reach the same answer for every case. Runners: internal/client/decisions_test.go (TestTheDecisionVectors) and web/decisions.ts (npm run decisions).

Each case is {name, kind, why, in, want}. `why` names the rule and the Go test the case restates. Each kind dispatches to exactly ONE function per language; no runner composes two, and no runner implements a rule of its own.

  close         in {status, preceding} -> want {verdict}. Go classifyClose; TS classifyClose(...).verdict. `status` null is "no close frame" (Go -1). `preceding` is a wire `error` frame decoded by the runner's GENERATED decoder, and one carrying a client_id is a malformed vector. verdict is reconnect | reconnect_at_maximum | terminal_protocol.
  threshold     in {access_issued_at, access_expires_at} -> want {threshold_ms}. refreshThreshold.
  due           in {access_issued_at, access_expires_at, clock_offset_ms, device_now} -> want {due}. refreshDue.
  delay         in {links} -> want {delay_ms}. refreshDelay.
  stamp         in {last_sent, now} -> want {stamp}. readStamp: missing or future is null.
  gate          in {answered_at, stamp} -> want {open}. gateOpen, over a stamp ALREADY read through readStamp.
  hold          in {links, answered_at, last_sent, now} -> want {hold}. refreshHoldAt, over a RAW last_sent. hold is none | unreachable | backoff.
  refused_hold  in {refused, links, last_sent, now} -> want {hold}. refusedHoldAt, over a RAW last_sent.
  chain         in {now, start, calls} -> want {refresh_token, chain, stamped, terminal}. The client's own refresh (Go Client.RefreshIfDue; TS RefreshingCredential.refreshIfDue), once per call, against a scripted /refresh.

CONVENTIONS. Instants are wire timestamps ("2026-09-19T12:00:00.000Z") or null for absent: the zero time.Time in Go, null in TS. Durations are integer milliseconds in fields named *_ms. A null access_expires_at means NO EXPIRY: the zero time in Go and NaN in TS, because StoredCredential.accessExpiresAt is a number and refreshDue reads a non-finite one as never due. That is the one translation a runner makes besides parsing instants; every other null passes through as the language's absent.

CHAIN TRANSCRIPTS. The credential starts from `start` (refresh_token, chain, last_sent) with its access token expired an hour before `now`, so a refresh is due, and the clock is fixed at `now`. Each call is one refresh; each step is one POST /refresh, in order. At every request the runner asserts: the presented (token, proposal); that the store ALREADY holds that link and a last_sent stamp (persisted before the request leaves); that every proposal is a valid wire Token (the request decodes through the generated decoder); and, after each call, that exactly its steps were consumed, no more and no fewer. `respond` is verbatim HTTP and no runner interprets it: {status, json} or {status, text}, optionally with headers (only "Retry-After": "0"), or {drop: true}, which closes the connection with no response (TS: the fetch rejects with a TypeError). After the last call the runner asserts `want` from STATE: the held refresh token, the chain, whether last_sent is present, and whether the client entered the CREDENTIAL terminal. Tokens are self-describing, low-entropy fixtures, as schema/vectors/vectors.json explains. $P1, $P2, ... name the proposals the client mints: a symbol BINDS ON FIRST APPEARANCE to what was presented, and every later appearance, in an expectation, a response or `want`, must equal it. `$` is outside base64url, so a symbol never collides with a fixture.

NO WANT NAMES A COUNTER. Stats, CredentialStatus counts, walk-backs and refused pages are not decisions, and Go and TS count differently under a fake clock (the /sync beside the first dial lands on the same instant as the pre-dial stamp). Transcripts pin what was presented and the end state only.

RUNNER CONTRACT, for CANT-42's Dart runner as for these two: an unknown kind FAILS, and so does a listed kind with no cases; symbols bind on first appearance; `respond` is written verbatim; a null expiry maps to the language's "no expiry"; `preceding` goes through the generated decoder; no counter is asserted. The Go runner also proves the file has teeth: a one-boundary mutant of each pure function, and the chain transcripts under Faults{NoChain} and Faults{ProposeAfresh}, must each fail at least one case.

NOT HERE. There is no backoff kind: CANT-170 ports CANT-35 ruling 3B to Go and adds it. The close case "1008 after error{<a code this wire version does not define>}" is left out until the Go client decodes it as the TS client does (CANT-177, which adds it). nextRefreshAt is not a kind: stamp and delay already pin it.

cases.name: close_4001
cases.why: The credential behind the session was revoked. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_4001_whatever_preceded_it
cases.why: 4001 is terminal whatever frame came before it. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1008_bare
cases.why: A bare 1008 is a client bug: replaying the same bytes walks into the same close. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1008_after_unauthorized
cases.why: The session was refused for its credential. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1008_after_wire_version_unsupported
cases.why: The server does not speak this wire version: update the app. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1008_after_internal_retryable
cases.why: error{internal} is never terminal and never eager. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1008_after_internal_not_retryable
cases.why: `retryable` is not consulted: a permanent server fault must not stop every client and keep them stopped after the fix. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1008_after_rate_limited
cases.why: 1008 preceded by an error carrying any other code reconnects with backoff. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1001_drain
cases.why: A drain reconnects. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1012_head_unreadable
cases.why: The server could not read its head; reconnect. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_4000_heartbeat_timeout
cases.why: A heartbeat timeout reconnects. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_4002_hello_timeout
cases.why: The hello timeout has closed 4002 since CANT-122 so that a bare 1008 could mean a client bug. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_no_status_abnormal_closure
cases.why: No close frame at all (Go -1, TS null): everything not listed reconnects. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1005_no_status_received
cases.why: A close frame with no status is "no status" (closeStatusKey counts it as -1) and reconnects. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1006_abnormal
cases.why: A browser reports an abnormal closure as 1006; "no status", and it reconnects. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1000_unlisted
cases.why: Unlisted: reconnects. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1009_unlisted
cases.why: Unlisted: reconnects. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_1011_unlisted
cases.why: Unlisted: reconnects. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: close_private_code_a_later_server_adds
cases.why: A code a later server adds reconnects: the default is the safe direction. Record §4; restates a row of TestTheCloseTableIsTheRecords (terminal_test.go).

cases.name: threshold_fifteen_minutes
cases.why: A person's fifteen minutes: a third is five. Record §1, max(60 s, a third of the served lifetime); restates TestTheThresholdIsAThirdOfTheServedLifetimeWithAFloor (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: threshold_exactly_at_the_floor
cases.why: Three minutes: a third is exactly the floor. Record §1, max(60 s, a third of the served lifetime); restates TestTheThresholdIsAThirdOfTheServedLifetimeWithAFloor (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: threshold_a_short_lifetime_is_held_up_by_the_floor
cases.why: Ninety seconds: a third is 30 s, and the floor holds it at 60 s. Record §1, max(60 s, a third of the served lifetime); restates TestTheThresholdIsAThirdOfTheServedLifetimeWithAFloor (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: threshold_an_hour
cases.why: An hour: a third is twenty minutes. Record §1, max(60 s, a third of the served lifetime); restates TestTheThresholdIsAThirdOfTheServedLifetimeWithAFloor (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: threshold_no_issue_time_gets_the_floor
cases.why: No issue time was ever learned: the lifetime is unknown, and the floor is the only number that does not guess it. Record §1, max(60 s, a third of the served lifetime); restates TestTheThresholdIsAThirdOfTheServedLifetimeWithAFloor (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_a_correct_clock_fresh
cases.why: A correct clock, a minute in. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_a_correct_clock_inside_the_last_third
cases.why: A correct clock, inside the last third. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_an_hour_fast_fresh
cases.why: An hour fast, fresh: not due, though the raw wall clock says long expired. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_an_hour_fast_inside_the_last_third
cases.why: An hour fast, inside the last third. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_an_hour_slow_inside_the_last_third
cases.why: An hour slow, inside the last third: due, though the raw wall clock says an hour left. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_an_hour_slow_fresh
cases.why: An hour slow, fresh. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_no_expiry_is_never_due
cases.why: No expiry was ever learned: there is nothing to measure against, and the reactive path is the net. The TS runner passes a null expiry as NaN. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_remaining_equal_to_the_threshold_is_not_due
cases.why: Five minutes left of fifteen is exactly the threshold, and due is LESS than it: an implementation comparing with <= refreshes early. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_a_third_that_is_not_a_whole_millisecond
cases.why: Issued T, expiring T + 900,001 ms: the threshold is 300,000.333… ms (Go: 900001000000 ns / 3), and at T + 600,001 ms exactly 300,000 ms remain, which is less, so due. An implementation that floors the third to whole milliseconds compares 300,000 < 300,000 and says not due. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: due_no_issue_time_uses_the_floor
cases.why: No issue time: the floor is the threshold, and 59.999 s left is inside it. Record §1: less than the threshold remains, on the server's clock (device time plus the persisted offset); restates TestDueIsDecidedOnTheServersClock (refresh_test.go).

cases.name: stamp_missing_is_absent
cases.why: A journal written before CANT-127 has no stamp. CANT-127's one rule for absent (readStamp; Go's Client.stamp delegates to it): missing and future are both absent. Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go), where absent and future stamps read as elapsed.

cases.name: stamp_in_the_future_is_absent
cases.why: A clock set backwards after the send: the stamp is later than now, and reads as absent. CANT-127's one rule for absent (readStamp; Go's Client.stamp delegates to it): missing and future are both absent. Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go), where absent and future stamps read as elapsed.

cases.name: stamp_equal_to_now_is_kept
cases.why: A stamp written this instant is not in the future. CANT-127's one rule for absent (readStamp; Go's Client.stamp delegates to it): missing and future are both absent. Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go), where absent and future stamps read as elapsed.

cases.name: stamp_in_the_past_is_kept
cases.why: The ordinary case. CANT-127's one rule for absent (readStamp; Go's Client.stamp delegates to it): missing and future are both absent. Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go), where absent and future stamps read as elapsed.

cases.name: gate_no_answer_with_a_stamp_is_closed
cases.why: A context that has heard nothing is closed. Record §3's gate (gateOpen): Catenary must have answered THIS context strictly later than the stamp. Restates TestAnAnswerNoLaterThanTheSendLeavesTheGateClosed and TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go).

cases.name: gate_no_answer_without_a_stamp_is_closed
cases.why: Closed either way: relaunch, a fresh push worker and a second tab are one property. Record §3's gate (gateOpen): Catenary must have answered THIS context strictly later than the stamp. Restates TestAnAnswerNoLaterThanTheSendLeavesTheGateClosed and TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go).

cases.name: gate_an_answer_and_no_stamp_is_open
cases.why: An absent stamp is opened by any Catenary answer: there is no send to be later than. Record §3's gate (gateOpen): Catenary must have answered THIS context strictly later than the stamp. Restates TestAnAnswerNoLaterThanTheSendLeavesTheGateClosed and TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go).

cases.name: gate_an_answer_equal_to_the_stamp_is_closed
cases.why: LATER THAN IS STRICT: an answer at the same instant as the send is closed, and the safe direction is one held attempt. Record §3's gate (gateOpen): Catenary must have answered THIS context strictly later than the stamp. Restates TestAnAnswerNoLaterThanTheSendLeavesTheGateClosed and TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go).

cases.name: gate_an_answer_later_than_the_stamp_is_open
cases.why: The gate opens on an answer after the send. Record §3's gate (gateOpen): Catenary must have answered THIS context strictly later than the stamp. Restates TestAnAnswerNoLaterThanTheSendLeavesTheGateClosed and TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go).

cases.name: gate_an_answer_before_the_stamp_is_closed
cases.why: Another attempt moved the stamp past the last answer, and the gate closes with it. Record §3's gate (gateOpen): Catenary must have answered THIS context strictly later than the stamp. Restates TestAnAnswerNoLaterThanTheSendLeavesTheGateClosed and TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_a_settled_credential_is_not_held
cases.why: Zero links: nothing to bound, whatever the gate says. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_a_closed_gate_inside_the_delay_is_unreachable
cases.why: The gate is checked first: no answer since the send reads as unreachable, even while the delay is also running. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_a_closed_gate_after_the_delay_is_unreachable
cases.why: The gate has no time: it opens on an answer, not on the clock. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_an_answer_equal_to_the_stamp_is_unreachable
cases.why: An answer at the same instant as the send does not open the gate. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_one_millisecond_before_the_delay_is_backoff
cases.why: The gate is open and 5 s have not quite passed since the send of a one-link chain. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_now_equal_to_stamp_plus_delay_has_elapsed
cases.why: now = stamp + delay: the wait is over. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_three_links_one_millisecond_before_20s_is_backoff
cases.why: Three links wait 20 s. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_three_links_at_20s_has_elapsed
cases.why: Three links wait 20 s, and at 20 s they have. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_a_future_raw_stamp_is_not_held_by_the_backoff
cases.why: A stamp in the future reads as absent: any answer opens the gate and the delay has elapsed. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: hold_a_missing_stamp_with_an_answer_is_not_held
cases.why: A chain written before CANT-127: any answer opens the gate, and absent reads as elapsed. CANT-127's two suppressors in order, the gate before the backoff (refreshHoldAt; Client.holdNow delegates to it). Restates TestTheGateIsDerivedFromTheStamp, TestABlackHoledRefreshIsBoundedByTheBackoff and TestAPersonCanSeeTheHold (hold_test.go).

cases.name: refused_hold_a_token_not_refused_is_not_held
cases.why: Nothing refused, nothing withheld. CANT-129: a refused token is presented once per refresh hold (refusedHoldAt; Client.refusedHold delegates to it). Restates TestARefusedTokenIsPresentedOncePerRefreshHold (refused_test.go).

cases.name: refused_hold_a_settled_credential_is_not_held
cases.why: Zero links: the chain collapsed because somebody got an answer. CANT-129: a refused token is presented once per refresh hold (refusedHoldAt; Client.refusedHold delegates to it). Restates TestARefusedTokenIsPresentedOncePerRefreshHold (refused_test.go).

cases.name: refused_hold_one_millisecond_before_the_delay_is_held
cases.why: Refused, one link, 5 s not quite passed. CANT-129: a refused token is presented once per refresh hold (refusedHoldAt; Client.refusedHold delegates to it). Restates TestARefusedTokenIsPresentedOncePerRefreshHold (refused_test.go).

cases.name: refused_hold_now_equal_to_stamp_plus_delay_has_elapsed
cases.why: now = stamp + delay: the one /sync goes out. CANT-129: a refused token is presented once per refresh hold (refusedHoldAt; Client.refusedHold delegates to it). Restates TestARefusedTokenIsPresentedOncePerRefreshHold (refused_test.go).

cases.name: refused_hold_a_future_raw_stamp_is_not_held
cases.why: ABSENT READS AS ELAPSED: a stamp in the future from a clock set backwards leaves the probe free to go. CANT-129: a refused token is presented once per refresh hold (refusedHoldAt; Client.refusedHold delegates to it). Restates TestARefusedTokenIsPresentedOncePerRefreshHold (refused_test.go).

cases.name: refused_hold_a_missing_stamp_is_not_held
cases.why: A chain written before CANT-127 has no stamp, which reads as elapsed. CANT-129: a refused token is presented once per refresh hold (refusedHoldAt; Client.refusedHold delegates to it). Restates TestARefusedTokenIsPresentedOncePerRefreshHold (refused_test.go).

cases.name: chain_a_newest_first_then_one_step_back_reusing_the_original_proposal
cases.why: Record §3: newest first, then ONE STEP BACK PER CATENARY 401, re-presenting the older token with the proposal it was FIRST sent with. The first request is lost; the next presents its proposal, which never existed, and the 401 steps back to the start token with $P1 again, which is answered. Restates TestAnUnknownOutcomeIsRecoveredByWalkingTheChain ("the first REQUEST never arrived") (chain_test.go).

cases.name: chain_b_a_hops_401_does_not_step_the_walk_back
cases.why: Record §5: a 401 that is not Catenary's (no {"code":"unauthorized"} body) says nothing about any token. It ends the attempt as an unknown outcome and never steps back to the start token, which may be spent. Restates TestAProxys401DoesNotStepTheWalkBack (chain_test.go).

cases.name: chain_c_a_200s_refresh_token_is_believed_over_the_proposal
cases.why: Record §3: THE RESPONSE'S refresh_token, NEVER THE PROPOSAL ON FAITH. A server that predates the field ignores the proposal and mints its own, and the client holds what it was given. Restates TestAServerThatIgnoresTheProposalIsBelieved (chain_test.go).

cases.name: chain_d_present_proposal_moves_the_walk_forward
cases.why: Record §5: 503 present_proposal says the rotation already committed. The client stops presenting that token and presents its proposal, with a new link of its own. Restates TestPresentProposalMovesTheWalkForward (chain_test.go).

cases.name: chain_e_fresh_proposal_rewrites_the_link_and_is_bounded_at_three
cases.why: Record §5: 503 fresh_proposal keeps the token and replaces its proposal, rewriting the link rather than extending the chain. Three times and no more: the fourth answer ends the attempt as an unknown outcome, not a terminal. Restates TestFreshProposalMintsAgainForTheSameToken ("a server that says it to everything") (chain_test.go).

cases.name: chain_f_catenarys_401_on_the_oldest_token_is_the_credential_terminal
cases.why: Record §5: only the OLDEST token's 401 is terminal. Two lost requests leave three links; a revoked device is refused at each, the walk steps back one per 401, and Catenary's refusal of the stored refresh token stops the client. Nothing is deleted: the credential and every link are kept. Restates TestARevokedDeviceWalksToTheOldestTokenAndStops (chain_test.go).

cases.name: chain_g_a_bare_503_is_an_unknown_outcome
cases.why: Record §5: a 503 that names no retry the client recognises is an unknown outcome, not an answer. The link stays, stamped. Restates TestAnUnknownOutcomeIsRecoveredByWalkingTheChain ("a 503 that names no `retry`") (chain_test.go).

cases.name: chain_h_a_relaunch_walks_the_persisted_chain_from_its_newest_proposal
cases.why: Record §3 across a kill: the chain is persisted before the request leaves, so a new process over the same store presents the persisted proposal first. Here the killed rotation committed, and it is answered. Restates TestAClientKilledMidRefreshRecoversOnRestart ("the rotation committed") (chain_test.go).

cases.name: chain_h_a_relaunch_steps_back_to_the_persisted_link
cases.why: Record §3 across a kill: the killed request never arrived, so its proposal does not exist. The 401 steps back to the start token, re-presented with the PERSISTED proposal, not a new one. Restates TestAClientKilledMidRefreshRecoversOnRestart ("the request never arrived") (chain_test.go).
